This vignette analyses a simulated series of trials in two stages, and then
fits a penalised regression of the trial means on trial-level covariates.

In the first stage each trial is fitted on its own and returns a mean for
each variety. The second stage models those means across trials. The means
are not equally precise: trials differ in their number of blocks and lost
plots. The second stage should therefore carry each mean's variance from the
first stage.

# The trials

Twenty trials, six varieties, three or four blocks per trial, and a few lost
plots. Four covariates are measured on each trial. `z1` shifts the trial
mean, and `z2`, `z3` and `z4` have no effect.


``` r
set.seed(20260920)

n_var <- 6L
n_trial <- 20L
trials <- sprintf("t%02d", seq_len(n_trial))

alpha <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = n_var)
z <- matrix(stats::rnorm(n_trial * 4L), n_trial, 4L)
colnames(z) <- paste0("z", 1:4)
trial_mean <- 4 + 1.2 * z[, "z1"] + stats::rnorm(n_trial, 0, 0.35)

plots <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_trial), function(i) {
  n_block <- sample(3:4, 1L)
  d <- expand.grid(
    variety = factor(paste0("v", seq_len(n_var))),
    block = factor(paste0("b", seq_len(n_block)))
  )
  d <- d[-sample.int(nrow(d), max(1L, floor(0.08 * nrow(d)))), ]
  b <- stats::rnorm(n_block, 0, 0.3)
  d$yield <- trial_mean[i] + alpha[as.integer(d$variety)] +
    b[as.integer(d$block)] + stats::rnorm(nrow(d), 0, 0.45)
  d$trial <- trials[i]
  d
}))

head(plots)
#>   variety block    yield trial
#> 1      v1    b1 4.031727   t01
#> 2      v2    b1 5.211888   t01
#> 3      v3    b1 4.944964   t01
#> 4      v4    b1 5.703127   t01
#> 5      v5    b1 6.137920   t01
#> 6      v6    b1 6.376713   t01
```

# Stage one: variety means per trial

`yield ~ 0 + variety` gives one mean per variety, and `random = ~block`
accounts for the blocks.


``` r
stage1 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(trials, function(tr) {
  dt <- plots[plots$trial == tr, ]
  dt$variety <- droplevels(dt$variety)
  fit <- flexybayes(
    yield ~ 0 + variety,
    random = ~block,
    data = dt,
    backend = "inla",
    verbose = FALSE
  )
  est <- tidy(fit)
  data.frame(
    trial = tr,
    variety = sub("^variety", "", est$term),
    ybar = est$estimate,
    v = est$std.error^2,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))

stage1$trial <- factor(stage1$trial)
stage1$variety <- factor(stage1$variety)
stage1 <- cbind(stage1, z[match(stage1$trial, trials), ])

rnd(head(stage1, 4))
#>   trial variety  ybar     v    z1     z2     z3    z4
#> 1   t01      v1 4.464 0.328 1.946 -0.898 -0.659 0.365
#> 2   t01      v2 5.353 0.407 1.946 -0.898 -0.659 0.365
#> 3   t01      v3 5.491 0.328 1.946 -0.898 -0.659 0.365
#> 4   t01      v4 5.640 0.328 1.946 -0.898 -0.659 0.365
round(range(stage1$v), 3)
#> [1] 0.083 0.902
```

`v` is the squared standard error of each mean, and it varies between trials.

# Stage two: carrying the variances

With `known_variance`, row $i$ has variance $\sigma^2 + v_i$: one residual
variance shared by all rows, plus the variance from the first stage.


``` r
base <- flexybayes(
  ybar ~ variety,
  random = ~trial,
  data = stage1,
  known_variance = stage1$v,
  backend = "inla",
  verbose = FALSE
)

rnd(tidy(base))
#>          term estimate std.error conf.low conf.high
#> 1 (Intercept)    2.864     0.401    2.072     3.656
#> 2   varietyv2    0.342     0.149    0.049     0.634
#> 3   varietyv3    0.775     0.148    0.484     1.066
#> 4   varietyv4    1.133     0.149    0.841     1.426
#> 5   varietyv5    1.637     0.149    1.344     1.930
#> 6   varietyv6    2.079     0.148    1.789     2.369
```

The simulated variety effects are 0.4 apart, so `v6` is 2.0 above `v1`.

# Carrying the full covariance of the first stage

The means of one trial share its block effects, so their errors are
correlated. `vcov()` of each stage-one fit gives their covariance, and
together the trials give a block-diagonal matrix with one row per mean.
Passed as `known_variance`, the matrix replaces the variances: row $i$ and
row $j$ have covariance $\sigma^2 [i = j] + K_{ij}$.


``` r
blocks <- lapply(trials, function(tr) {
  dt <- plots[plots$trial == tr, ]
  dt$variety <- droplevels(dt$variety)
  fit <- flexybayes(
    yield ~ 0 + variety,
    random = ~block,
    data = dt,
    backend = "inla",
    verbose = FALSE
  )
  v <- vcov(fit)
  rownames(v) <- colnames(v) <- paste(tr, sub("^variety", "", rownames(v)))
  v
})
K <- matrix(0, nrow(stage1), nrow(stage1))
key <- paste(stage1$trial, stage1$variety)
for (v in blocks) {
  at <- match(rownames(v), key)
  K[at, at] <- v
}

base_k <- flexybayes(
  ybar ~ variety,
  random = ~trial,
  data = stage1,
  known_variance = K,
  backend = "inla",
  verbose = FALSE
)

rnd(data.frame(
  term = names(coef(base)),
  variances_only = coef(base),
  full_covariance = coef(base_k)
))
#>                    term variances_only full_covariance
#> (Intercept) (Intercept)          2.864           2.835
#> varietyv2     varietyv2          0.342           0.413
#> varietyv3     varietyv3          0.775           0.785
#> varietyv4     varietyv4          1.133           1.175
#> varietyv5     varietyv5          1.637           1.612
#> varietyv6     varietyv6          2.079           2.132
```

The matrix is fitted on INLA only, and brms stops with
`known_variance_not_supported`.

# Penalised selection on the whitened design

Penalised regression is a well-grounded way to choose among candidate
covariates: the lasso and the elastic net shrink the coefficients of
covariates that do not improve the fit to exactly zero. Its usual software
assumes independent rows, and the trial means are not independent: means
from one trial share its random effect and their first-stage errors. The
fitted model gives their covariance $V$, and with $V = U^\top U$ its Cholesky
factor, $U^{-\top} y$ and $U^{-\top} X$ have independent errors of variance
one. A penalised regression on these whitened values is generalised least
squares with a penalty.

`fb_marginal_cov()` returns $V$ for the fitted model, here the model with the
full first-stage covariance, and `as.matrix()` makes it dense. The variety
columns are the part of the model that is not penalised, and the four trial
covariates are the candidates.


``` r
V <- as.matrix(fb_marginal_cov(base_k))
U <- chol(V)

X_variety <- stats::model.matrix(~ variety, stage1)
Z <- as.matrix(stage1[, c("z1", "z2", "z3", "z4")])

y_w <- backsolve(U, stage1$ybar, transpose = TRUE)
X_w <- backsolve(U, cbind(X_variety, Z), transpose = TRUE)
colnames(X_w) <- c(colnames(X_variety), colnames(Z))
```

glmnet then fits the lasso path. The whitened intercept is not a constant
column, so it enters as one of the unpenalised columns and glmnet fits no
intercept of its own. The folds hold out whole trials. Whitening mixes rows
only within a trial, because $V$ is block-diagonal by trial.


``` r
penalised <- c(rep(0, ncol(X_variety)), rep(1, ncol(Z)))
fold <- as.integer(stage1$trial) %% 5L + 1L

set.seed(20260920)
cv <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(
  X_w, y_w,
  penalty.factor = penalised,
  intercept = FALSE,
  foldid = fold
)
round(as.matrix(stats::coef(cv, s = "lambda.1se"))[colnames(Z), , drop = FALSE], 3)
#>    lambda.1se
#> z1      0.359
#> z2      0.000
#> z3      0.000
#> z4      0.000
```

The lasso keeps `z1`, the covariate with an effect, shrunk towards zero, and
sets the other three to zero. Here one $V$, estimated from all trials,
serves every fold. To keep the held-out trials out of $V$ as well, refit the
model on each fold's training trials with `fb_refit()` and whiten with that
fold's $V$.
